draft.title: Entropy
card: Entropy (S) measures how spread out the energy and the particles of a system are. The more ways they can be arranged, the higher the entropy.
Gases have more entropy than liquids, and liquids have more than solids. Particles in a gas are far apart and move freely.
Entropy rises when a solid melts, a liquid boils, or a solid dissolves in water. It also rises when a reaction makes more moles of gas.
Entropy falls when the change goes the other way, such as a gas condensing or fewer moles of gas forming. The change in entropy is written ΔS. It is positive when entropy rises.
draft.remember: More spread out and freer to move means higher entropy.

a.q: Which change has a positive ΔS?
opts: Carbon dioxide gas turning to dry ice
a.why: Liquid water is more spread out than ice, so entropy rises. The other three changes make particles more ordered, so entropy falls. Condensing is tempting, but it moves from gas to liquid.
a.clue: Which change frees the particles to move more?

b.q: Which reaction has the largest increase in entropy for the system? 2H2O2(l) → 2H2O(l) + O2(g) is one option.
b.why: The first reaction makes a gas from liquids, so the particles become far more spread out. The other three use up gas or form a solid or liquid, so entropy falls. The ammonia reaction is tempting, but it turns four moles of gas into two.
b.clue: Look for a reaction that makes gas, not one that uses it up.

problems.detail: The stem says '2H2O2(l) → 2H2O(l) + O2(g) is one option.' Singling out the correct option in the stem draws attention to it and gives the answer away. Remove that sentence.

Why (b) calls the correct answer 'the first reaction', but the options are shuffled and it appears third here. Name the reaction (hydrogen peroxide decomposing) instead. 'Makes a gas from liquids' should also be 'from a liquid', since there is only one reactant.

The card says entropy rises when a solid dissolves in water. That is usually true, but some ionic solids have a negative entropy of solution because water molecules become ordered around the ions. 'Usually rises' would be more accurate.

problems.detail: Why (a) says liquid water is 'more spread out than ice'. Water is an exception: liquid water is denser than ice, so its molecules are closer together.
